sections.title: CP4: Mode 2 retrieval on D4
sections.question: Do hybrid search and reranking find the vulnerable function among a release range's changed functions better than simple baselines?
caveats: BM25, dense and hybrid retrieval are statistically indistinguishable on this data; the paired intervals include zero.
Rerankers do not help; the code-search embedder is worse than bge-small.
Retrieval only ranks the candidates a range contains; it cannot recover a labelled function that is not a candidate.
The advisory-ID control is weak: no query contains an advisory ID.

sections.title: CP5: LLM selection (E1, S1) and HyDE
sections.question: Does a local LLM improve on (E1) predicting every changed function of a fix commit, (S1) the retriever's top-1, and does a hypothetical-document query (HyDE) improve retrieval?
sections.interval: cluster-bootstrap (clusters by fix commit or release range)
caveats: E1: choosing one function from a fix diff lowers recall against the baseline that keeps all of them; a wrong narrowing is the error that could cause a false NOT_REACHABLE later.
S1: one model improves on top-1 only when it answers; the other abstains often because the frozen prompt invites abstention; this measures instruction following, not code understanding.
HyDE: at most one of many comparisons excludes zero, with no correction for multiple comparisons; not a finding.
Headline groups use cases created after each model's documented training cutoff; where no cutoff is documented, every dated case counts as possibly seen.

sections.title: CP5b: lifting and caller/callee queries
sections.question: Can walking up the call graph from a changed internal function to its exported callers recover the functions the advisory names, and can graph expansion rescue the Mode 2 ceiling?
sections.interval: cluster-bootstrap (D1 clusters); counts for the ceiling
caveats: Lifting ran with go1.26.10 fetched into a scratch directory because many modules need a newer Go than CI; the lifting evaluation is not reproducible inside CI.
Neither lifting rule is good enough to sit inside the verdict path; it is a candidate-widening aid only.
E1+L beats E1 by adding symbols, but nothing beats the E0 baseline; it does not rescue the LLM pick.
The D4 ceiling investigation has a tiny n; the graph tools are an ablation, not a promised gain.

sections.title: CP6: the LangGraph investigation agent (Mode 2)
sections.question: Does an agent that can read diffs and walk callers/callees pick the vulnerable function better than the retriever's top-1 (A0), and at what cost?
caveats: The agent does not beat plain retrieval (A0). Any win is over the one-shot LLM baseline, which mostly did not answer for one model.
Cost is about five times the prompt tokens and about twice the seconds of the one-shot LLM.
The frozen loop rule ended many runs without an answer for one model; whether a looser rule helps was not tested and must not be tuned on D4.
Headline wording was fixed before results; the failure analysis is a purposive sample, so its cause counts are not rates.

sections.title: CP7: end-to-end triage and the evidence verifier
sections.question: Does the whole pipeline (two reachability methods, the verdict rule table, the verifier, the Mode 2 policy) give correct verdicts where the truth is known, and how does it behave on real modules?
caveats: Fixture accuracy is measured against truth by construction; the D1 and D4 rows are verdict distributions on real modules analysed as their own application, not accuracy.
Mode 2 shows false REACHABLE verdicts on the fixtures by construction (an unrelated function changed in the same range is reachable), so Mode 2 answers are candidate level.
Mode 2 numbers here ranked candidates with BM25, the documented fallback, not the intended hybrid retriever.
Most CANT_DETERMINE verdicts on real modules come from modules needing a newer Go than the review toolchain and from libraries with no main package.

sections.title: CP7b: real applications (D3), adjudicated
sections.question: On real Go applications, are the REACHABLE paths real, are the NOT_REACHABLE verdicts safe, and how does the official govulncheck compare?
caveats: REACHABLE means a call-graph path exists from a main package and needs a human look; it is never exploitability and, here, never confirmed.
The adjudication was done by two Claude reviewer agents reading the source, reconciled by the supervising assistant, with an owner spot-check of path steps; it is not expert human ground truth.
The path-feasibility figure judges the path shown, not whether the target is reachable by another path.
On these cases the official tool was not worse than this pipeline.
Analysis ran with go1.26.10 on the review machine (outside CI); n is small, from few applications, so intervals are wide.
